summary.headline: Singer India Q1 FY27 revenue rose 57% to Rs 144.5 crore and EBITDA rose 330% to Rs 5.5 crore, with sewing machines up 74%.
summary.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue up 57% to Rs 144.5 crore, PBT up 225% to Rs 4 crore and EBITDA up 330% to Rs 5.5 crore. Sewing machines grew 74% and the trade channel grew more than 25%, while appliances grew about 15% but its segment result fell by about Rs 74 lakh YoY on EPR costs and organisation build-out. Management said a sharp commodity price rise disrupted demand and sourcing in the quarter. Working capital absorbed cash for ZigZag and industrial machine imports and inventory, with closing cash at about Rs 58 crore.

financial_highlights.metric: Operating cash before working capital changes

segments.name: Sewing machines
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 74% in Q1, with the trade channel up more than 25%, e-commerce up more than 55% and ZigZag machines up more than 20%. Revenue mix in the quarter was about 20% ZigZag, 50% black machines and 30% industrial machines and accessories.

segments.name: Appliances
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 15% from trade expansion, e-commerce and fans, but segment result fell about Rs 74 lakh YoY on EPR and organisation build-out. Fans grew about 61%; coolers underperformed while induction cooktops helped.

guidance_outlook: Management aims for EBIT-level breakeven in appliances, which it now expects next year rather than this fiscal.
Bhiwadi, Rajasthan factory on track for pilot production in the second half of FY27, initially focused on ZigZag machines, with initial capacity of 10,000+ machines per month.
Kendriya Bhandar order (Rs 202 crore) targeted for completion by end of the quarter; the contract has a 25% volume scale-up clause.
Industrial sewing machine growth expected to be high in coming periods, though Q1 was damped by a steep price correction.
Dividend policy not addressed; management said the Board is aware of investor expectations.
capex_capacity: Bhiwadi factory is being set up as asset light at first, focused on skill building, then in-house component manufacturing, then industrial sewing machines.
Advances of about Rs 14.3 crore to Singer Sourcing LLC for ZigZag machine imports and about Rs 4 crore for industrial machine imports, at 30% advance with 70% on bill of lading.
Total inventory and import deployment of about Rs 32 crore in the quarter, plus inventory build in fans.
New Jammu factory has started making Made-in-India ZigZag machines compliant with the revised BIS standard IS 15449.
demand_pricing: Commodity price spike caused demand disruption, labour shortage and sourcing challenges; a steep price correction was taken, which dampened demand in appliances and industrial machines.
Management says it is gaining market share, with consistent growth across channels and categories.

Revised BIS standard IS 15449 took full effect on 12 August 2026; management says Singer is the only company manufacturing ZigZag machines to the new standard in India and no further NOCs or imports will be allowed.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Kendriya Bhandar order's pending balance and scale-up potential clear?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to complete the order by quarter end and declined to give the pending value, citing competitive sensitivity. It said a 25% volume expansion and a larger future tender are possible but depend on government decisions.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EPR cost and why are appliances profits weak?
qa_highlights.answer: EPR is about Rs 1.2 crore for the quarter, which is proportionate for the year and relates to past sales. Management aims for appliances EBIT breakeven and expects it to cover the cost.

qa_highlights.question: How much cash was generated and what is the cash balance?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating cash before working capital changes was Rs 4.35 crore. About Rs 32 crore went into inventory and import advances, and closing cash is about Rs 58 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 100 crore surplus enough for inorganic growth and the factory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is open to inorganic deals but will only pursue good opportunities. The factory will be built in stages, and it said more funds will come if needed.

qa_highlights.question: Why import ZigZag machines when local manufacturing has started?
qa_highlights.answer: Imports were allowed until 12 August. The Rs 14.3 crore of advances was described as de-risking inventory while domestic production ramps up.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue split and export plan?
qa_highlights.answer: The mix is about 20% ZigZag, 50% black machines and 30% industrial machines and accessories. Exports are a lower priority than India, though SVP Global may buy machines for its global supply chain.

risks_watch: Commodity cost inflation and price corrections may keep dampening demand in appliances and industrial sewing machines.
Appliances profitability depends on EPR costs (about Rs 1.2 crore per quarter) and on reaching EBIT breakeven, now guided for next year.
ZigZag manufacturing learning curve: management says the capacity ramp is still in progress, and the import stock build reflects that.
Working capital absorbed cash in Q1, so cash conversion needs watching.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and market share, especially sewing machines, but cautious on appliances profitability and industrial machine demand. Management avoided giving numbers on the Kendriya Bhandar order balance and dividend policy.
key_quotes: we are the only Company who are manufacturing these machines as per new standards in India.
We are very cautious of the fact that even though we have cash, it's precious cash and it will be deployed with full responsibility
Our goal is to become very quickly EBIT breakeven. But I think that's going to happen next year.

adds.what: Bhiwadi, Rajasthan factory initial capacity 10,000+ ZigZag machines per month (asset-light start, pilot production)

growth.why: Q1 revenue +57% and EBITDA +330% with sewing machines +74%, backed by a Rs 202 crore Kendriya Bhandar order and a Bhiwadi factory targeting 10,000+ ZigZag machines/month from pilot production in H2 FY27, though no company-wide revenue guidance was given and the commodity-driven price correction dampened appliances and industrial machines.
